public_rationale: The claim says reliable reasoning about time and prices needs a 'proper model', and that without one, answers are only superficial. Marcus does not say what counts as a proper model or where 'superficial' ends and 'reliable' begins. Whether LLMs build internal world models is itself disputed, so no system can be agreed to be on either side of the line. Temporal-reasoning benchmarks exist, but they do not sort systems by world-model presence. With no plain reading to test, the claim is not adjudicable.
limitations: The claim is a theoretical argument about cognition rather than a measurable statement.
Performance on temporal benchmarks alone cannot test a necessity claim about internal models.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Without a proper world model, an AI system cannot reliably reason about time, inflation, or changing prices, only superficially.

statement.excerpt: Without a proper model, you can’t possibly reliably reason about time, and affiliated concepts like inflation and changing prices. A model might be able to answer queries about time, but only superficially.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.
